 On Friday, the network launched its annual ‘Countdown to Christmas’ event, rolling out the first of 34 new holiday-themed movies

 On Friday, the network launched its annual “Countdown to Christmas” event, which reached 38 million unique viewers during last year’s holiday season. 
 Across nine weeks, the network will roll out a record 34 new films, including a third installment of the “Holiday Touchdown” series and a movie inspired by a Brad Paisley song. 
 Here are Hallmark’s 34 new movies for the 2026 holiday season. 
 ‘’Tis the Season for Setups’ 
 An organized party planner and an easygoing ski instructor join forces to play matchmaker for their single parents, only to discover unexpected chemistry at the ski resort. 
 Premieres: Friday, Oct. 16
 ‘Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story’ 
 Avery, an ambitious reporter, returns home to Chicago for the holidays, where she profiles Darlene Donnelly, a Chicago Bears superfan attending her 500th game. With help from Darlene’s charming grandson, Avery discovers the magic of football, family and home. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Oct. 17
 ‘Mr. & Mrs. Christmas’ 
 A single dad moves his family to a charming small town weeks before the holidays, where he tries to create Christmas magic for his two daughters at the town’s beloved Christmas market with help from a local woman. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Oct. 18
 ‘Winter Wonderlanes’
 A pop-up restaurateur returns home for Thanksgiving to save her grandfather’s bowling alley, Wonderlanes, reluctantly accepting help from her high school boyfriend. 
 Premieres: Friday, Oct. 23
 ‘Forgotten Holiday’ 
 After an antiques buyer’s boyfriend surprises her with a pre-Christmas proposal, he is in a car wreck that leaves him with no memories of their relationship or his love of Christmas. She must retrace their relationship for him to revive their relationship. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Oct. 24
 ‘What If Christmas’
 After being gifted a magical Christmas ornament, Erin wakes up in an alternate reality where she followed her dreams of becoming a successful fashion designer — in exchange for feeling lonely at Christmas. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Oct. 25
 ‘Who’s Coming For Christmas?’ 
 Using pieces she inherited from her grandmother, Julie sets her Christmas Eve table for eight guests — without any guest on her list. With a little faith and a Christmas miracle, she hopes to fill her seats with family, friends and a burgeoning love interest. 
 Premieres: Friday, Oct. 30
 Related Television is finding its second life on YouTube ‘Adopting St. Nick’ 
 A Christmas Companions program at the local retirement community brings together a single mother and a jolly man with an uncanny resemblance to Santa Claus. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Oct. 31
 ‘A Danish Christmas’ 
 When returning to her family’s Copenhagen inn, Marie mistakes a handsome guest for a travel writer and gives him the ultimate Danish holiday experience in hopes of saving the floundering inn. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Nov. 1
 ‘Merry Memories’ 
 Michaela, a rigid accountant, steps in to help with her nephew, Danny, over Christmas while his mother is deployed. 
 When Danny is given a school assignment to create a holiday scrapbook for his mom, Michaela accepts help from a free-spirited teacher, who teaches her how to embrace imperfection and open her heart. 
 Premieres: Friday, Nov. 6
 ‘Holiday Unplugged’ 
 When a server wipes out treasured photos of Sally’s late husband, she decides to hunt down the original tapes with help from a charming expert who offers help her recover the memories. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Nov. 7
 ‘A Season of Promises’
 Two sisters reunite to prepare their single father to return to the dating scene, hoping he will find someone special before Christmas, while also going on their own journeys that bring them unexpected joy. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Nov. 8
 ‘My Christmas Cowboy’ 
 After a TV hosts has an on-camera gaffe, he leaves Hollywood for Texas to keep a low profile. Once there, he must relearn his old cowboy skills for the upcoming Reindeer Roundup from a local news producer who still resents him for taking her job in college. 
 Premieres: Friday, Nov. 13
 ‘The Nights Before Christmas’ 
 A bit of holiday magic lands a man in a time loop. He decides to use the extra time charming a beautiful journalist and break the spell — but every morning, she can’t remember who he is. 
 Premieres: Friday, Nov. 14
 ‘Mistletoe and Mimosas’ 
 When a big-city business woman unexpectedly inherits her Uncle Lou’s Christmas-themed bar, The Tipsy Reindeer, she returns to her small hometown to save it from a rival bar owner. They agree to competing in a series of festive challenges — and the winner gets to decide on the future of the bar. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Nov. 15
 ‘Our Holiday Playbook’ 
 Lexi strikes a deal with a local former football star, who agrees to pose as her boyfriend and help her team win in her family’s annual Christmas flag football showdown.
 Premieres: Friday, Nov. 20
 ‘Christmas in Blue Dog Valley’ 
 A Hollywood veterinarian moves to a small town to take over a family-run veterinarian clinic, where she finds herself falling in love with the tight-knit community and an unexpectedly charming resident. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Nov. 21

 Identical twins Abigail and Charlie travel to Wales to run a bookshop for Christmas, where they both meet someone special. But mistaken identities and holiday mix-ups complicate their burgeoning romances. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Nov. 22
 ‘Christmas Delivered’ 
 While spending the holidays with her grandmother, Kimberly uses her tech expertise to help save a local tree farm, while also sparking some holiday romance with the farm’s owner. 
 Premieres: Thursday, Nov. 26
 ‘The Christmas Eve Feast’ 
 Disillusioned with her job as an executive chef at a swanky city restaurant, Silvy returns to participate in her family’s beloved “Feast of the Seven Fishes” Christmas Eve dinner.
 While prepping, she finds unexpected romance with a local photographer, and a renewed love for cooking. 
 Premieres: Friday, Nov. 27
 ‘Return to Santa’ 
 Decades after his letter to Santa Claus was misplaced, Jake’s life is turned upside down as his childhood wishes become a reality in his current life — as well as the unexpected return of his childhood best friend, Julie. 
 Premieres: Friday, Nov. 27
 ‘The Most Wonderful Secret’ 
 A burned-out art teacher visits her brother for Christmas, where she is selected for the town’s “Secret Norma” holiday scavenger hunt. While also trying to revive the town’s Christmas block party, she rediscovers her love of teaching art while falling for a charming electrician. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Nov. 28
 ‘Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True’ 
 Lindsey’s dream of spending the holidays with her family at Disney World goes awry when she discovers her hotel room is next door to the man she recently went out with on a disastrous first date. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Nov. 28
 ‘Eight Nights for Love’ 
 A magical antique menorah transports a woman back to eight pivotal moments throughout her life. After visiting old memories, she begins spending more time with her best friend, Ethan, and discovers she has long buried her feelings for him. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Nov. 29
 ‘Miles To Christmas’ 
 When a snowstorm disrupts Cassidy’s holiday flight plans, she joins a pair of free-spirited siblings on a road trip to the nearest airport to find different flights. Along the way, unexpected feelings begin to emerge. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Nov. 29
 ‘The Snowflake Effect’
 Tanya inadvertently triggers a magical antique snowflake’s bad luck curse when she gifts it at a White Elephant party. To break the curse, she teams up with a laid-back gift shop clerk to track down the snowflake and reverse her luck. 
 Premieres: Friday, Dec. 4
 ‘A Grand Biltmore Christmas’
 After reuniting with her childhood best friend, Michael, at a Christmas Eve party in 1895, Elizabeth is transported to the modern world. There, Michael reveals he is a time traveler. 
 As the two of them get close to a magical Christmas, Elizabeth must choose between the life she is building in the present and the one she already has in the past. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Dec. 5
 ‘An Angel In My Stocking’
 Years after the end of her brief marriage, Amanda winds up stranded with her ex-husband in a small, snowbound Vermont town. With help from her guardian angel, Amanda is given a second chance at love. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Dec. 6
 ‘Christmas in Canterbury’ 
 Rose, an American choir director, travels to Canterbury, England, for the holidays, where she unexpectedly takes over the local children’s choir, competing for a spot in the annual Christmas Eve concert in Canterbury Cathedral. 
 Premieres: Friday, Dec. 11
 ‘Snow Globe Town’ 
 Emily joins her sister on a Christmas getaway to Pine Grove, a town known for its romantic proposals. To participate in the town’s couples-only events, Emily is paired with Bert, a skeptical journalist investigating the town’s love-obsessed traditions. 
 Premieres: Saturday, Dec. 12
 ‘Noelle Nomads’ 
 When Joseph and his daughter’s Hawaiian holiday plans are derailed by a fender-bender at an RV park, a free-spirited woman helps them embrace the freedom of camp life. Now falling in love, Joseph must choose to stick to his plans or follow his heart. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Dec. 13
 ‘Hearts All Aglow’ 
 A music historian and a big-city attorney cross paths at a Christmas gala, both hoping for an opportunity to connect with the same legendary musician. They decide to join forces and discover what they are searching for might not be the thing they truly need. 
 Premieres: Friday, Dec. 18
 ‘Barking All The Way’ 
 An overworked real estate agent’s Christmas plans take an unexpected turn when she agrees to watch over a chaotic-yet-lovable dog, who reunites her with her high school sweetheart. 
 4 Comments Premieres: Saturday, Dec. 19
 ‘Save the Date for Christmas’ 
 Hopeless romantics and longtime friends Susie and Alec agree to take a break from attending weddings, until Susie’s sister announces her own last-minute Christmas wedding. 
 While navigating wedding duties together, the pair discover a new appreciation for love and marriage. 
 Premieres: Sunday, Dec. 20
